items.question: Cover Letter
items.problem:
Expected "I build internal tools for problems I actually run into. The clearest example is jobright-application-agent, a Playwright and TypeScript agent I built to handle the repetitive browser work in job applications. The hard part was not automation, it was restraint: one wrong action can submit a real application or fill a legal field incorrectly. So I put every application through an explicit state machine, used SQLite as the single source of truth because browser state diverging across processes is how these systems silently break, and gated every mutating capability behind fail-closed flags that never default on. I also built a validation ladder from unit-confirmed to live-mutation-confirmed, because passing against a local fixture does not mean a capability works. Free-text and demographic fields always escalate to a human. Workday and iCIMS are detected and skipped rather than handled unreliably.

That is the mindset I would bring to developer-productivity work with AI coding agents in a monorepo: figure out where the agent should act, where it should stop, and how you prove it works. I have also built LLM evaluation systems before, comparing model outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard at Intelehealth to surface systematic failure modes. I would like to do this full time in Redwood City."; page shows "(empty)"
